chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who misses the Witr prayer; he said, 'He makes it up as Witr always.'

key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: Witr, the odd-numbered night prayer performed after Isha
key_terms.يَقْضِيهِ: He makes it up / compensates for it

ai.seo_question: How should one make up the missed Witr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the juristic principle of *qada* (making up) for the Witr prayer is clarified, emphasizing that the missed prayer must be performed as a single, odd-numbered unit to preserve its distinct identity as a *mustahabb* (recommended) prayer with specific characteristics. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that Witr, while not obligatory in the same strict sense as the five daily prayers, retains its unique legal status requiring a specific mode of compensation. The emphasis on 'always' (*abadan*) underscores the consistency required in maintaining the ritual integrity of this night prayer.
